 Equitas SFB MD & CEO P N Vasudevan resigns citing perception of conflict of interest, stock down 20%
 Vasudevan will continue as MD & CEO until a successor takes over
 By BL Chennai Bureau 
 Updated - October 29, 2026 at 04:07 PM. × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/equitas-sfb-md-amp-ceo-p-n-vasudevan-resigns-citing-perception-of-conflict-of-interest-stock-down-20/article71640049.ece Copy 
 PN Vasudevan
 | Photo Credit:
 BIJOY GHOSH
 Equitas Small Finance Bank on Thursday informed exchanges that its MD and CEO PN Vasudevan has resigned, and the Board has taken note of the resignation at its meeting today. 
 While the company in its statement notes that Vasudevan is stepping down to pursue certain personal and social initiatives, in his resignation letter, the banking veteran says that he is resigning to remove an “overhang” on the stock because of perception of conflict of interest arising from his daughter co-promoting an NBFC licensed by RBI in 2023. 
 “In my investor meetings over the past 3 years, I have been repeatedly asked about the perceived conflict of interest. In reality there is no conflict of interest, since there is no transaction at all between our bank and the said NBFC…” he said. 
 Explaining to Investors
 “Inspite of my explaining the above to investors, the perception of conflict continues to persist. I am told by investors that this ‘overhang’ is causing the stock to underperform, impacting value creation for both shareholders and employees,” he added. 
 “Sometimes perceptions are stronger than reality. Under the circumstance, it is important that we remove the ‘overhang’ arising out of the perception issue,” he added. 
 The issue relates to Vasudevan’s daughter co-founding Unico Housing Finance even as the former was MD and CEO of Equitas. 
 Succession Plan
 He adds that about 40 years in the industry, he also wants a break to build a corpus for his trust and focus on a different segment of society. Reports suggest that Reserve Bank of India (RBI) initiated an inquiry into Equitas Small Finance Bank earlier this year, and the regulator is said to have questioned board members on whether they were fully aware of this relationship when extending Vasudevan’s tenure as MD. 
 Vasudevan will continue as MD & CEO until a successor takes over and the Board has asked the Nomination and Remuneration Committee to identify internal and external candidates. The Board said it does not expect any impact on the bank’s long-term vision. 
 The shares of Equitas SFB were trading at ₹52.04, down over 20 per cent on the BSE at the time of writing.
